name: Eyes Closed
description: Vasya and Petya were tired of studying so they decided to play a game. Before the game begins Vasya looks at array a consisting of n integers. As soon as he remembers all elements of a the game begins. Vasya closes his eyes and Petya does q actions of one of two types: 1) Petya says 4 integers l 1, r 1, l 2, r 2 — boundaries of two non-intersecting segments. After that he swaps one random element from the [ l 1, r 1] segment with another random element from the [ l 2, r 2] segment. 2) Petya asks Vasya the sum of the elements of a in the [ l , r ] segment. Vasya is a mathematician so he answers Petya the mathematical expectation of the sum of the elements in the segment. Your task is to write a program which will answer the second type questions as Vasya would do it. In other words your program should print the mathematical expectation of the sum of the elements of a in the [ l , r ] segment for every second type query.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n , q ( 2 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 , 1 ≤ q ≤ 10 5 )  — the number of elements in the array and the number of queries you need to handle. The second line contains n integers a i ( 1 ≤ a i ≤ 10 9 )  — elements of the array. The next q lines contain Petya's actions of type 1 or 2. If it is a type 1 action then the line contains 5 integers 1, l 1, r 1, l 2, r 2 ( 1 ≤ l 1 ≤ r 1 ≤ n , 1 ≤ l 2 ≤ r 2 ≤ n ). If it is a type 2 query then the line contains 3 integers 2, l , r ( 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ n ). It is guaranteed that there is at least one type 2 query and segments [ l 1, r 1], [ l 2, r 2] don't have common elements.
output_specification: For each type 2 query print one real number — the mathematical expectation of the sum of elements in the segment. Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error doesn't exceed 10 - 4 — formally, the answer is correct if where x is jury's answer and y is yours.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 895E — Eyes Closed [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
